title: Cross-SDK elastic-batch scheduler + ergonomic streaming shim for embeddings + rerank
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: deliver a cross-language helper that provides deterministic, cost-efficient pagination and adaptive batching for embeddings and reranking workflows, plus ergonomic streaming wrappers for Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs.
Problems addressed: (1) customers writing custom scroll/batch loops across SDKs have divergent behavior (ordering, retries, backoff), (2) rerank flows often need deterministic cursor semantics when results are split across pages, and (3) streaming ergonomics differ widely between sync/async languages which leads to leaked KV cache or unclosed connections.
Scope: - Implement an "elastic-batch" scheduler that adapts batch size based on recent latency and token throughput per model instance. - Provide cursor-first pagination semantics (cursor token is opaque but stable for rerank order) with optional deterministic sort keys for datasets where ordering matters. - Expose retry profiles optimized for embeddings (idempotent) vs rerank (idempotent but ordering-sensitive) with configurable jitter and per-language defaults. - Add ergonomic streaming shims: lightweight context-managed generator for Python, async iterable for TS, and channel-based streamer for Go. - Deliver cross-sdk examples and end-to-end test harness that validates equivalence of output ordering and retry behavior across languages.
Non-goals: instrumenting runtime kernel selection or autoscaling policies (handled elsewhere).
Design notes: - Chose cursor-based pages (cursor token + page_size) over offset indexes because offsets break when underlying indexing or caching prunes items; cursor supports stable continuation and plays well with KV caching and prefix reuse. - Elastic-batch logic: start with conservative batch_size=8, probe up to 64 by doubling when 95th-percentile latency < latency_target and throughput budget allows. Probe decay window is 30s. Operators can pin batch_size in SDK config. - Retry profiles: embeddings: exponential backoff with max_retries=4, base_delay=200ms, max_delay=3s. Rerank: more conservative backoff with max_retries=3 and a short circuit path for deterministic fallback to smaller batch sizes when persistent 429s are observed. - Streaming shim responsibility: ensure underlying request handles are closed on consumer cancellation/exception and expose a small buffer for prefetching one batch to reduce tail latency.
Migration notes: - Existing SDK pagination helpers will be deprecated in favor of this shim; add a migration guide showing 1-2 line rewrite for each SDK.
Success criteria: - Parity tests pass: for 3 canonical datasets, outputs match across Python/TS/Go when running with identical input sequences and mocked model backends. - Performance: average per-token cost decreases by at least 8% for batchable workloads compared to baseline non-adaptive batching. - Developer experience: docs + examples added, and early adopter feedback from 2 customers validates ergonomics.
updates: 2025-02-13 - Kickoff: scoped core APIs and agreed on cursor-based pagination rather than offset; assigned language leads (Marco for Python/Go, Linh for TypeScript).

2025-02-14 - Spike: implemented prototype elastic-batch algorithm in a playground repo; observed 12% cost savings on synthetic workload. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-playground/pull/112

2025-02-16 - Design review: PM and Design requested clearer cancellation semantics for streaming; decided to add context-manager pattern for Python and explicit Close() on Go streamer. Review notes: https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/c/STREAM-DESIGN-9

2025-02-18 - Engineering sync: settled on retry defaults (embeddings: 4 retries, rerank: 3 retries) and added opt-in deterministic-sort parameter for rerank pages. Draft API doc pushed: https://docs.redwood.ai/sdk/elastic-batch-shim

2025-02-19 - Tests: wrote end-to-end parity test harness that runs against mock backend; initial run shows ordering drift in TypeScript when handling 429s — root cause is per-request retry window not preserving cursor mapping. Created follow-up task ENG-61258 to harden TS retry wrapper.
2025-02-20 - PR opened for Python shim with examples and migration guide: https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/pull/789; requested review from @emily (DX) and @sanjay (runtime).
testing_notes: Parity harness runs: - 3 datasets (news-snippets, support-threads, product-descriptions) - Mocked backend that can inject 429, 503, and variable latency - Assertions: set-equality of rerank outputs per input query and identical continuation cursors when not mutated intentionally. Added stress test to ensure streamer cleanup on consumer cancel. TODO: add chaos test injecting out-of-order cursor responses from backend.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal dogfood: enable opt-in flag in SDK alpha channels for 2 internal teams. 2) Beta: invite two external customers for early feedback, monitor logs for migration errors and cost delta. 3) GA: flip default to on with deprecation notice for old helpers. Metrics to track: per-request retries, average batch_size, per-token cost, ordering mismatches (should be 0%).
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: backend systems returning inconsistent cursors could cause silent ordering issues. Mitigation: detect cursor anomalies in SDK and raise an explicit error in verbose mode. Risk: adaptive batching may overshoot and increase tail latency. Mitigation: conservative probe policy + operator pinning. Risk: cross-language parity gaps. Mitigation: shared test harness and canonical fixture dataset checked into repo.
acceptance_criteria: - API docs and examples for Python/TS/Go exist and show 1-line migration. - Parity tests pass for canonical datasets in CI. - Python PR merged and TS/Go PRs at least opened and in review. - Telemetry emits batch_size and retry_count for >95% of calls.
